successCriteria.description: The Employee entity type exposes exactly the canonical fields with correct types: id: string, employeeNumber: string, firstName: string, lastName: string, email: string, managerId: string | null, department: string | null, hireDate: Date, terminationDate: Date | null, employmentStatus: EmploymentStatus, createdAt: Date, updatedAt: Date, deletedAt: Date | null.

The repository exposes all seven operations — findById, findByEmployeeNumber, findByEmail, findByManager, create, update, softDelete — and each read returns a mapped Employee (or null/empty list) while each write persists and returns the affected Employee.

create persists a new employees row using parameterized SQL with a RETURNING clause, generates id via randomUUID(), sets createdAt/updatedAt to now, and returns the mapped Employee; update and softDelete (setting deletedAt) likewise return the mapped result.

Write methods accept an optional PoolClient as the last parameter and use it when supplied (shared pool untouched), falling back to the shared pool when omitted; read methods always use the shared pool.

The service is a thin delegating facade over an injectable IEmployeeRepository (defaulting to the concrete EmployeeRepository) and forwards each repository operation, including the optional client for writes.
Jest unit tests exist under tests/unit/modules/employee/ covering repository SQL/params/row-mapping/optional-client behavior and service delegation, and the full suite passes (npm run build + jest).

constraints: All database access uses raw pg parameterized SQL against the shared pool exported by src/shared/db/connection.ts; no Knex in repository queries, no inline SQL outside the repository layer.

The service owns the unit-of-work boundary and never imports a pool/client/module-level db helper; it receives IUnitOfWork via injection and passes the acquired client to participating repository methods as the optional last parameter.

Strict TypeScript (no implicit any, strict null checks); use unknown with type guards rather than any (the audit module's Record<string, any> jsonb precedent does not apply to Employee — no jsonb fields here).

The module mirrors the committed audit module structure: model (entity + input), repository (IEmployeeRepository + EmployeeRepository), service (IEmployeeService + EmployeeService), and index.ts as the sole public entry point; no circular dependencies.

The input interface omits generated fields (id, createdAt, updatedAt, deletedAt) and includes employeeNumber, firstName, lastName, email, managerId, department, hireDate, terminationDate, employmentStatus.
outOfScope: DDL/migrations for the employees table — repositories assume the table already exists; no migration files are produced in this phase.
HTTP controller/routes, API-boundary validation, and RBAC wiring for the employee module — no controller or routes files are created in this phase.
package.json dependency pruning/renaming and creation of src/index.ts — neither is required for this phase's build (tsc --noEmit + jest).

entityInvariants.invariant: employmentStatus is always one of the EmploymentStatus enum values (ACTIVE | INACTIVE | TERMINATED); no other lifecycle state is representable.
managerId is a self-referential FK to employees.id and may be null (no manager); it is never a dangling reference to a non-existent employee.
employeeNumber and email are unique across all non-deleted employees; softDelete marks deletedAt rather than physically removing the row, so a soft-deleted employee's unique values remain reserved.
id, createdAt, and updatedAt are generated by the repository (never caller-supplied); deletedAt is null until softDelete and terminationDate is null while the employee is not terminated.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Rejects with a typed error when a unique constraint (employee_number or email) is violated; otherwise persists and returns the created Employee.
Return the mapped Employee or null when no matching row exists; never throw for a missing record.
Returns the (possibly empty) list of employees whose managerId equals the given id; never throws for an empty result.
Persists the supplied changes and returns the updated Employee; a missing target row surfaces as a typed not-found error rather than a silent no-op.
Sets deletedAt (and updatedAt) on the target row and returns the soft-deleted Employee; a missing target row surfaces as a typed not-found error.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Reuse the EmploymentStatus enum (ACTIVE | INACTIVE | TERMINATED) exactly as exported — do not redefine or duplicate it.
Import the shared pg Pool (and PoolClient type) from the shared-db public entry point; never construct a new pool.

Match the employees table mapping: snake_case columns (employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) with PK id, FK manager_id -> employees.id, and unique indexes on employee_number and email.
Mirror the audit module's repository pattern: a snake_case row interface plus a mapRow function converting DB rows to the camelCase entity, randomUUID() for id generation, and RETURNING on insert.

Mirror the audit module's service pattern: injectable repository defaulting to the concrete implementation, thin delegation, and the I*Service interface naming convention (IEmployeeService, not EmployeeServiceInterface).

Follow the transaction contract: the service owns the unit of work and receives IUnitOfWork via injection; repository write methods take the optional PoolClient as the last parameter and fall back to the shared pool when omitted.

integrationPoints.why: The Employee entity's employmentStatus field is typed against this enum; the module must import it from the shared-types entry point.
The repository issues all queries against this shared pool and accepts PoolClient for transactional writes.
The service owns the transaction boundary and receives IUnitOfWork via injection to acquire the client passed to participating repository writes.
